core_job: For people whose phones hold the same contacts several times over from iCloud, Gmail, Exchange and SIM imports: find every set of cards that describe one person, even when the names differ or the cards are in different accounts, show the evidence for each match, and fix them safely in place. Today the app finds groups (real union-find on phone, email and name in lib/domain/contact_duplicates.dart) but the user cannot do anything with them: the cards have no merge, dismiss, open or export action, and nothing is saved between launches. The identical-photo finder (SHA-256, keeps one copy) stays as a secondary tab.
signature: Cross-account match plus merge with a restore point, all on-device. Each card shows which account it lives in (flutter_contacts 2.5.0 Contact.metadata.accounts), and groups that span accounts are flagged. A merge first exports every original card to a vCard file in the app's Application Support directory and aborts if that save fails; only then does it update the kept card and delete the others. A Restore points list puts the originals back with one tap (into their original account, or the default account with a notice) and can share the .vcf file. Distinct because, per Apple's and Google's own help pages fetched with curl today: iOS Contacts merges only cards with the same first and last name (support.apple.com/guide/iphone/iph2ab28320d), and Google Contacts cannot merge contacts saved in different Google accounts (support.google.com/contacts/answer/7078226). Paid third-party cleaner apps: competitor not verified, because web search was disabled in this session.

must_fix: Double restore creates duplicate contacts. contact_merger.dart:213 restore() never checks point.restoredAt, and the Restore button at restore_points_screen.dart:222 is always enabled. Proof: in a temporary copy of HEAD outside the repo (since deleted), a probe test using the repo's fakes merged g1+i1 and then called restore twice. It printed `QA first=2 second=2 log=[create:Jane Smith@jane@gmail.com, create:Mom@iCloud, create:Jane Smith@jane@gmail.com, create:Mom@iCloud]`. Fix: refuse or disable a second restore once restoredAt is set (or show 'Already restored'), and add a test for it.
